newsitem.title: GERMANY: Toepfer sees tight EU feeds market for rest of '96.
newsitem.headline: Toepfer sees tight EU feeds market for rest of '96.

text.p: Most animal feeds should remain tight and expensive this year in northwest Europe, where livestock industries are covering their winter demand, trader Alfred C Toepfer said on Friday.
Higher overseas shipments of palmkernel cake and copra products, fishmeal and citrus pellets were expected to offer some relief from early 1997 onwards, it said in a monthly report.
But soybean and meal supplies would remain tight until the arrival of Latin American crops in the spring, as EU consumers were competing with internal U.S. demand and Chinese buying.
Corngluten prices, along with those of citrus pellets, were seen underpinned by good dairy feed mixer demand.
Thai tapioca prices had firmed due to ship delays and December auctions looked set to produce even higher prices.
Cane molasses prices remained steady amid slow sales extank and domestic beet molasses prices were pointing downwards.
Bucking the overall trend was corn germ meal which piled up in Rotterdam ports after Brazil quickly exported a backlog of months' worth of supply, Toepfer said.

A newsletter from the local office of the American Soybean Association (ASA) expected downward pressure on corngluten prices after estimates of a higher U.S. maize crop and reports of ample southern European maize harvests.
The ASA also said tight domestic rapeseed meal markets were partially balanced by some imports from China.
